title: Adaptive spatial and frequency experts fusion network for medical image fusion

architecture_backbone: Spatial and Frequency Experts Fusion (SFEF) module

contributions.improvement: adaptively fuse local features and improve the details of the fused images
contributions.implementation_detail: A cross attention spatial fusion (CASF) module is devised to adaptively fuse local features, which can constraint the consistency in spatial correlations by crossing the self-similarity map between two source images.

contributions.improvement: fuse global features, reduce computational complexity, and overcome the influences of the limited field of view on the fusion results
contributions.implementation_detail: An adaptive frequency fusion (AFF) module is introduced to fuse the features from a global perspective in frequency domain through a simple CNN architecture with spatial attention.

contributions.improvement: adaptively fuse local and global features, and further improve the quality of fusion images
contributions.implementation_detail: An ensemble-learning-based spatial and frequency experts fusion (SFEF) module is used, taking the fused features in spatial and frequency domains as two experts.

contributions.improvement: significant performance improvements on various medical image fusion tasks and superiority in downstream disease classification task

limitations: Large number of parameters and huge computational complexity (FLOPS) compared to CNN-based models.

Fusion weights are still dependent on the hyperparameters in the loss function and modules, investigating the method to set these hyperparameters adaptively is still a challenging and interesting work.

datasets.details: 184 pairs of CT-MRI images, 269 pairs of PET-MRI images, and 357 pairs of SPECT-MRI images. For each dataset type, 24 image pairs were randomly selected as the test set, with the remaining pairs used as the training set. All images are 256 × 256 pixels. PET and SPECT images are color images with RGB channels, whereas CT and MRI images are single-channel grayscale images. For PET-MRI and SPECT-MRI image fusion tasks, PET and SPECT images were initially converted to the YCbCr color space, using the Y channel for training and combining Cb and Cr channels for final fusion result.

experiment_setup.training_details: Implemented using the PyTorch framework on an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. AdamW [34] optimizer with default parameters (β₁ = 0.9, β2 = 0.99, weight_decay = 0.2). Learning rate is 2×10-4. Number of epochs was set to 2000. Batch size was set to 4. Loss function hyperparameters λ = 0.5 and η = 0.5. CASF module patch size p = 16, embedding dimension = 256. AFF module number of MLPs m = 4, number of slots s = 256. Encoder convolutional layers share parameters across different modalities. For downstream classification task, SGD optimizer was used, training epoch = 100, batch size = 16, initial learning rate = 1×10-3.
